prompt: Ruben, the pricing analytics manager, sets this take-home task on dunnhumby's Breakfast at the Frat, a public dataset of weekly store sales, and asks how units under each promotion tactic compare with weeks of no promotion in each product category. Use every week in the data, from the week ending 14 January 2009 to the week ending 4 January 2012. Each sales row is one product in one store for one week. Class it by its flags: 'feature and display' when feature and display are both 1; 'feature only' when feature is 1 and display is 0; 'display only' when display is 1 and feature is 0; 'price reduction only' when tpr_only is 1 and feature and display are both 0; and no promotion when feature, display and tpr_only are all 0, whatever the price, a missing price included. A row with tpr_only 1 that is also featured or on display takes its class from feature and display alone. Return one row for each category and tactic that has at least one sales row, leaving weeks of no promotion out, with six columns in this order: category; tactic, one of the four labels above; product_store_weeks, the number of sales rows; avg_units, the average units per sales row; no_promo_avg_units, the average units per sales row of no promotion in the same category; and units_diff_pct, 100 times (avg_units minus no_promo_avg_units) divided by no_promo_avg_units, rounded to 1 decimal, and missing when no_promo_avg_units is 0 or missing. Leave the two averages unrounded. Sort by category, then tactic, both from A to Z.
hints: Next, give each sales row its category and its tactic label, then find each category's average units in weeks of no promotion.
Group the labelled rows by category and tactic, and join each group to its category's no-promotion average before you work out the difference.
why_this_works: Classing each row once, with feature and display checked before tpr_only, keeps a row with clashing flags in one tactic, and each category's own no-promotion average is its baseline.
